short: In-domain EEG pretraining adds 4.3 points on 24 mouthed words (35.3% to 39.6%), one session, no seeds; Du-IN showed this earlier. Muscle artefact and new users remain untested.
position: The paper changes training (M03) and the decoder (M06); both are standard against the field. Pretraining on about 105 h of the same 12 participants' unlabeled EEG raises 24-word accuracy from 35.3% to 39.6%, a relative gain similar to the one Du-IN reported earlier for 61-word sEEG with six seeds, here from one test session per participant without seeds or tests. The headline 7.3-point margin over TCNet also contains an architecture gain from a far larger model. Mouthed articulation leaves facial muscle activity uncontrolled, the semantic mean is misprinted as 42.8% in §5.1 against 47.0% in Table 2, and transfer to new users or datasets, which the 'large brain language model' label implies, is not tested.
